newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans convention authority mulls swap.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans convention authority mulls swap.

text.p: New Orleans Exhibition Hall Authority is considering a $100 million interest rate swap on revenue bonds issued last year to fund convention center expansion, authority Chief Finance Officer Dave Ohlmeyer said Monday.
The authority is reviewing a swap proposal from Raymond James & Associates Inc, Ohlmeyer said.

"We have not made any decisions whatsoever. We're just in a very, very early state of discussing it," Ohlmeyer said. "We would be looking at targeted savings of annual interest around the 50 basis point range."
The complicated swap would be from fixed-rate to variable, with a second variable-to-fixed component, Ohlmeyer said.

The revenue bonds were issued last year for the third phase of expansion of the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center. The expansion is scheduled for completion in February 1999 and will increase exhibition space from 700,000 square feet to 1.1 million square feet.
Ohlmeyer said construction is about two months ahead of schedule.
Last week, the State Bond Commission approved a $70 million line of credit ahead of pending bond issuance for the state's share of funding for the project.

The state agreed to issue $35 million of general obligation bonds each year in fiscal 1997, 1998 and 1999. No bonds were sold in 1997, so the state will issue $70 million of GO bonds for the project this year as part of Louisiana's annual bond issue to cover appropriations.
